system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Framing note:** The Seller's cover describes these as "key negotiated positions" and the funds flow as reflecting "agreed price mechanics". Nothing in our file supports that any of these have been agreed, and no Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback. Treat every item as the Seller's opening position. Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (§§2, 3, 5, 10) undercuts several of its SPA positions – we should use it.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% is our conditional fallback only and no Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three limbs.** Seller's figures are 5x ours and the deductible structure would permanently strip AUD 250,000 from every recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a rider that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; the "applies to all Claims" rider deleted.
- Recommendation: **Reject; hold 24 months and delete the rider.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the rider is a back-door general-regime override (see SPA-N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Title to the shares is the entire consideration for AUD 24m; a 20%/18-month limit on it is not simplification, it is a transfer of fundamental risk.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and Schedule 7.** This is a non-waivable playbook position and the Seller's drafting purports to cap even fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2; Sch 7).
- Buyer wants: specific fair disclosure only; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters a prudent search would reveal.
- Recommendation: **Reject §1.1 and §1.2; require specific disclosures against identified warranties with a fair-disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure would hollow out the warranties and effectively make the 20% cap a cap on nothing.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: blanket exclusion for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete cl 8.3. If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons, mirrored by a Seller knowledge definition with named persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is an unbounded constructive-knowledge test that doubles up the general disclosure point and would defeat claims we are entitled to bring.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter §2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: a Completion condition requiring effective, unconditional Bluefen consent AND evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, with Seller obliged to procure (not merely use reasonable endeavours).
- Recommendation: **Reject; hard condition precedent with consent plus satisfied-conditions evidence.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a consent subject to unmet conditions is not a consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter §3 confirms not repaid and no discharge in the data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed security releases/discharges delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking AND Amelia Frost approval; neither is on offer, and on a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and uncertain change-of-control (cl 8.1) exposure.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter §5 confirms exclusion and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) either (a) a specific line item in the funds flow paid/deducted at Completion, or (b) expressly Seller-funded with an indemnity.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require a specific funds-flow line item (gross of on-costs) or a Seller-funded indemnity.** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company – i.e. the Buyer – pays post-Completion, which contradicts cash-free/debt-free.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter §4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: a broader indemnity covering loss from non-ownership/non-transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims and remediation cost, while preserving the cure (pay SOW3 fees, obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion).
- Recommendation: **Reject as inadequate; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion cure or an escrow.** The exposure is loss of title to deliverables, not just the AUD 180,000 fee – and that figure is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter §6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- Buyer wants: Seller obligations to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide updates to Completion, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident if it crystallises; warranty that the disclosure is complete. Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "not material" label; add preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** We must assume NO confirmed breach, harm or notification duty in either direction, so the correct tool is process and contingent protection, not a price adjustment.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter §8: silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008/DD-011 to be read together for timing/scope.
- Buyer wants: DD-008 and DD-011 reviewed together to confirm timing, terminability and whether any amounts are accrued but unpaid at Completion; no automatic Debt classification or price reduction.
- Recommendation: **Assess, do not concede.** Neither "ordinary course" nor "Debt" is established on the record; put the question to the Seller and reserve the working-capital/Debt treatment pending answers.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: a general rider that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", and limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each as discrete categories with their own cap, time limit and threshold treatment, expressly outside the general regime.
- Recommendation: **Delete the rider and the "all Claims of any nature" language; insert an express hierarchy clause.** This is the mechanism by which SPA-N-004, -005 and -016 would be silently collapsed into the 20%/18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter §10 concedes this merely identifies the Seller's source and does not say the Buyer has verified it.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extracts and historical company search, constitution, share certificates, board minutes/authorities for the Seller and Company, PPSR and security searches, and a title/capacity/no-encumbrance warranty plus completion deliverables.
- Recommendation: **Reject DD-012 as sufficient; run independent title and encumbrance searches and require the full completion deliverables set.** A register the Seller controls is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms remain OPEN and negotiated separately (separate caps, periods and basis – tax warranties/indemnity typically running to statutory limitation periods; IP given the Ironquay issue).
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; mark Tax and IP as open with placeholders.** No resolution has been reached, and we should neither accept the general regime nor assume unlimited liability.

---

**Priority items for the next mark-up / principal escalation:** SPA-N-004, -005 and -014 (structural), SPA-N-008 and -009 (completion mechanics on ~AUD 6.8m of combined exposure), and SPA-N-010 (funds flow). None of the fallbacks in -001, -003 or -009 can be offered without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
